title: Cap. IV Arg. 4 Sol: in Christo refers to the electing act — Eph. 1:3, 2 Cor. 5:19 parallels
pass_a_gloss: For those words, in Christ, are to be referred not to the state of the elect man, but to the act of the electing God. The Arminians so expose, He chose us in Christ, that is, Us existing in Christ, or us considered and foreseen as believing in Christ, and inserted into him through faith, God afterward chose. But this form of speaking, in Christ, as often as it is joined with some Divine act, does not always hint that the subject toward which that act tends is considered as existing in Christ antecedently. For example, Eph. 1:3. God blessed us with every spiritual blessing in Christ. But among spiritual blessings is the very first donation of faith and repentance, which are not given to those existing in Christ, but to those alien from Christ, that they may be led to Christ, and inserted into him. So God is said in Christ to have reconciled the world to himself, 2 Cor. 5:19; in Christ to have created us unto good works, Eph. 2:10. Finally the Remonstrants themselves teach that God regenerates men in Christ, Coll. p. 99. In all these places those words, in Christ, cannot except most absurdly be exposed as existing in Christ antecedently. To elect therefore in Christ is nothing else than in electing to look to Christ the Mediator and Head of the Church, and by his grace to destine members to be joined to him and glorified.
pass_b_english: In Christ refers not to the elect man's state but to the electing God's act. Arminians expose He chose us in Christ as: us already existing in Christ, or foreseen as believing and inserted by faith, whom God then chose. But in Christ joined to a divine act does not always mean the subject already exists in Christ beforehand. Eph. 1:3: God blessed us with every spiritual blessing in Christ — and among those blessings is the first gift of faith and repentance, given not to those already in Christ but to those alien from him, to bring them to Christ and insert them. So God in Christ reconciled the world to himself (2 Cor. 5:19) and created us unto good works (Eph. 2:10). Remonstrants themselves say God regenerates men in Christ (Coll. p. 99). In all these, in Christ cannot without absurdity mean already existing in Christ beforehand. So to elect in Christ is nothing but, in electing, to look to Christ the Mediator and Head of the Church, and by his grace to destine members to be joined to him and glorified.
source_text: Nam illa verba, in Christo, non ad statum hominis electi, sed ad actum eligentis Dei sunt referenda. Arminiani sic exponunt, Elegit nos in Christo, id est, Nos existentes in Christo, vel nos consideratos et praevisos ut credentes in Christum, et per fidem in illum insertos, Deus postmodum elegit. Sed haec loquendi formula, in Christo, quoties conjungitur cum aliquo actu Divino, non semper innuit subjectum, in quod tendit ille actus, considerari ut existens in Christo antecedenter. Verbi causa, Eph. i. 3. Deus benedixit nobis omni benedictione spirituali in Christo. At inter spirituales benedictiones est ipsa prima fidei et poenitentiae donatio, quae non dantur existentibus in Christo, sed alienis a Christo, ut ad Christum adducantur, et ei inserantur. Sic Deus dicitur in Christo mundum sibi reconciliasse, 2 Cor. v. 19; in Christo ad bona opera nos condidisse, Eph. ii. 10. Denique ipsi Remonstrantes docent Deum regenerare homines in Christo, Coll. pag. 99. In hisce omnibus locis verba illa, in Christo, non possunt nisi absurdissime exponi, in Christo antecedenter existentes. Eligere igitur in Christo nil aliud est, quam in eligendo respicere ad Christum Mediatorem et Caput Ecclesiae, ejusque gratia membra illi conjungenda et glorificanda destinare.
